coverage.authoredAnalysis: Cover and publisher identity; no explicit election date or printed page.
Retrospective 2019-2023 achievements and commitment to further action. Housing-law/rent-limit references describe achievements; do not automatically treat them as a new unconditional proposal.

Employment: 45-day dismissal compensation, reinstated processing wages, priority for Basque/provincial/autonomous collective agreements, 32-hour working week without salary or condition reductions; targeted measures for women/youth. Minimum wage proposal continues on page 4.

Minimum wage of 1,200 euros and ability to supplement a local minimum to 60% of average wage; no pay-period/gross-net assumption. Basque/Navarre labour framework, labour-inspection and passive-employment transfers; interim inspector staffing. Housing: indefinite automatic lease-renewal extension preserving rent and conditions; mortgage intervention limited by loan amount, interest-rate reversal and a 15% maximum increase.

Banking good-practice obligations and wider access; 1,080-euro minimum pension, further widow/non-contributory increases, no rise in retirement age or calculation period, social-security economic-regime transfer. Food-chain controls and distribution-profit tax; gas-price cap maintained until prices return to pre-rise levels.

Community heating tariff. Health: resident-doctor places, repeal of Law 15/1997, mental-health budget and resident-psychologist places, public optical/basic dental care, free menstrual products for vulnerable people and reduced VAT. Permanence/funding for transport subsidies, Renfe/Feve investment and local-rail transfers.

Permanent basic-supply protection for vulnerable households; benefit-reference index linked to price rises above 2.5%, 15% higher vulnerability income thresholds, broader minimum-income access and at least 12% higher amounts; simpler and in-person administrative procedures.

Permanent higher bank/energy/large-fortune taxes with foral administration; supermarket-profit tax repeated, not a separate measure. Oppose/reverse ECB rate rises, oppose fiscal-rule social cuts, repeal constitutional Article 135 amendment, social/cooperative recovery programme and SME-centred industry law; mandatory return of aid when firms relocate production.

Higher 2030 decarbonisation goals and climate neutrality in 2040; planned renewable investment with territorial conditions; EU electricity-price-system reform; public electricity retail firms; water saving/control/agricultural innovation and sanctions for irregular energy-company reservoir use. Alleged causal effects are party arguments, not established quiz consequences.
Feminist rights and equality across jobs/pay, pensions and care; broad LGTBIQ+ rights protection. Broad goals do not establish a precise numerical stance on every existing law.

Anti-discrimination and representation of LGTBIQ+ people; replacement of immigration law, safe migration/asylum routes and Irun-Hendaia reopening; end immediate returns; comprehensive anti-racism law.

Public-security-law repeal with specific changes: respect/disobedience offences, rubber bullets and immediate returns; external independent police oversight. Inclusive memory, coexistence and recognition/justice/reparation for victims including torture, state terrorism and far-right groups.
Replace official-secrets law to improve access and accountability, linked to unresolved historical deaths.
Plurinationality, recognition of Euskal Herria, political dialogue and right to decide; respect parliamentary agreements ratified by citizens. Does not specify an unconditional unilateral procedure.

Basque-language access to state administration, protection of education models, digital/audiovisual promotion and respect for other languages. All pending autonomy transfers, prioritising social/economic powers; list continues on page 16.

Complete transfer list: benefits, local rail, migration, labour framework, ports/airports. Protect autonomy against recentralisation and transfer new relevant measures; bilateral, transparent and equal negotiation of Basque/Navarre fiscal arrangements. Publisher footer; no further annex or footnote.
